properties.description: The image builds, runs unprivileged, and a design survives replacing the container (run by hand on a real Docker daemon, 2026-08-06, 6 checks): builds clean on BOTH bases (ubuntu:22.04 the release base, ubuntu:24.04 the dev fallback); the container reaches `Up (healthy)`, so the HEALTHCHECK's /dev/tcp probe works and the port is only bound after the store is open; `id` inside reports uid 1000 on both bases; the volume gets the designed layout with graph.id.json and graph.meta.json BESIDE the store rather than inside it; and THE ACCEPTANCE TEST FROM req:hosted-state-outlives-the-image PASSES — stop the container, start a new one against the same volume, and graph_id is byte-identical (4934a26b7cc87ed2 both times) with ZERO re-mint warnings, so the new container adopted the existing design rather than opening an empty one beside it. WHAT THIS DOES NOT COVER, stated because the gap is invisible otherwise: the release.yml `container` job has never run — publishing needs a version tag — so registry login, push, multi-tag and the pull-back verification are unexercised. The Dockerfile is proven; the publish path is written and untested.
properties.name: The image builds, runs unprivileged, and a design survives replacing the container
